chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'A person will not be in poverty (while observing) moderation'.

key_terms.اقْتِصَادٍ: Moderation, frugality, or economy in spending
key_terms.عَالَ: To be in poverty or destitution

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between moderation in spending and avoiding poverty according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa ibn Bakr narrates that Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) succinctly teaches that moderation (*iqtisad*) in expenditure prevents poverty, emphasizing that it is not the lack of wealth but the lack of management that leads to destitution. This hadith is foundational in Shia ethical economics, linking spiritual discipline with financial prudence, and is often cited alongside the concept of *wasatiyyah* (moderation) as a core Islamic virtue. The term *iqtisad* here implies a balanced approach to life, avoiding both extravagance and stinginess, thereby ensuring long-term stability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Musa Bin Bakr who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A person will not be in poverty (while observing) moderation’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “
Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘With moderation, one does not suffer poverty.’”
